1	# Independent Analysis of AI Models and API Providers -- Artificial Analysis, April 2026
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	- URL: https://artificialanalysis.ai/
     6	- Captured: April 10, 2026
     7	
     8	Artificial Analysis is an independent platform that benchmarks large language models across intelligence, speed, and pricing. The data below reflects the latest evaluations published in April 2026, covering both proprietary and open-weight models from major AI labs worldwide.
     9	
    10	## Intelligence Index: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 Share the Lead at 57
    11	
    12	The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is a composite score aggregating performance across a wide range of reasoning, knowledge, and instruction-following benchmarks. Higher scores indicate stronger overall capability.
    13	
    14	As of April 2026, two models share the top position:
    15	
    16	| Rank | Model | Provider | Intelligence Index |
    17	|------|-------|----------|--------------------|
    18	| 1 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | Google | 57 |
    19	| 2 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | OpenAI | 57 |

    25	| 8 | Gemini 3 Flash | Google | 46 |
    26	| 9 | DeepSeek V3.2 | DeepSeek | 42 |
    27	| 10 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | NVIDIA | 36 |
    28	| 11 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | OpenAI | 33 |
    29	
    30	Google and OpenAI are neck-and-neck at the frontier. Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 trails by 4 points, while Meta's newly released Muse Spark enters at a strong 52. Open-weight models such as GLM-5.1 and Grok 4.20 occupy the mid-tier, demonstrating that the gap between proprietary and open-weight models continues to narrow.
    31	
    32	![Intelligence Index ranking of top AI models, April 2026](./assets/chart_intelligence_index_ranking.jpg)
    33	
    34	## Output Speed: Open-Weight Models Dominate Throughput
    35	
    36	Inference speed, measured in output tokens per second, is critical for latency-sensitive applications. The leaderboard shows a striking pattern: open-weight and smaller models generate tokens far faster than frontier proprietary models.
    37	
    38	| Rank | Model | Output Tokens/s |
    39	|------|-------|-----------------|
    40	| 1 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | 218 |
    41	| 2 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | 188 |
    42	| 3 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | 172 |
    43	| 4 | Gemini 3 Flash | 153 |
    44	| 5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 118 |
    45	| 6 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | 83 |
    46	| 7 | GLM-5.1 | 64 |
    47	| 8 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | 63 |
    48	| 9 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | 49 |
    49	| 10 | DeepSeek V3.2 | 46 |
    50	
    51	The fastest model, gpt-oss-120B (high), outputs 218 tokens per second -- more than 4x the speed of Claude Opus 4.6 and nearly 5x that of DeepSeek V3.2. This highlights the trade-off between raw intelligence and throughput: the two intelligence leaders (Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4) sit in the middle of the speed table at 118 and 83 tokens/s respectively.
    52	
    53	![Output speed ranking by tokens per second](./assets/chart_output_speed_ranking.jpg)
    54	
    55	## Pricing: A 33x Gap Between Cheapest and Most Expensive
    56	
    57	API pricing per million tokens varies enormously across models, reflecting differences in compute requirements, margin strategies, and competitive positioning.
    58	
    59	| Rank | Model | USD per 1M Tokens |
    60	|------|-------|--------------------|
    61	| 1 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    62	| 2 | DeepSeek V3.2 | $0.30 |
    63	| 3 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | $0.40 |
    64	| 4 | Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 |
    65	| 5 | GLM-5.1 | $2.10 |
    66	| 6 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | $3.00 |
    67	| 7 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | $4.50 |
    68	| 8 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | $5.60 |
    69	| 9 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | $6.00 |
    70	| 10 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | $10.00 |
    71	
    72	The cheapest options -- gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 at $0.30 per million tokens -- are over 33x less expensive than Claude Opus 4.6 at $10.00. For budget-sensitive workloads, this price differential is a decisive factor. Notably, Gemini 3 Flash offers a compelling mid-range value at $1.10, pairing solid speed (153 tokens/s) with reasonable intelligence (46).
    73	
    74	![Price per million tokens comparison across models](./assets/chart_price_per_million_tokens.jpg)
    75	
    76	## The Intelligence-Throughput Frontier: Finding the "Most Attractive Quadrant"
    77	
    78	A scatter plot of Intelligence Index versus output tokens consumed during evaluation reveals which models occupy the "most attractive quadrant" -- high intelligence with efficient token usage. Models that achieve high scores while consuming fewer tokens represent better engineering and more efficient architectures.
    79	
    80	Key observations from the scatter plot:
    81	
    82	- Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and DeepSeek V3.2 cluster in the upper region, indicating strong intelligence scores.
    83	- Grok 4.20 0309 v2 and several Google models sit in the middle-right region, balancing intelligence and token efficiency.
    84	- Llama 4 Maverick occupies the low-intelligence, low-token region, suggesting it is neither efficient nor highly capable.
    85	- MiMo-V2-Pro appears in the upper-right corner, showing very high intelligence but with substantial token usage.
    86	
    87	![Scatter plot of intelligence index vs output tokens, highlighting the most attractive quadrant](./assets/chart_intelligence_vs_output_tokens.jpg)
    88	
    89	## Proprietary vs. Open-Weight Models
    90

GLM-5.1, an open-weight model from Z AI, scores 51 -- just 6 points behind the co-leaders. Meanwhile, open-weight models like gpt-oss-120B dominate on speed and price. The intelligence leaderboard includes models from at least 8 distinct organizations across the US, China, and Europe, reflecting a genuinely global competition.

    93	| Metric | Proprietary Leader | Score | Open-Weight Leader | Score |

    95	| Intelligence | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 57 | GLM-5.1 | 51 |
    96	| Speed (tokens/s) | Gemini 3 Flash | 153 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | 218 |
    97	| Price ($/1M tokens) | Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    98

   100	
   101	- **Two-way tie at the top**: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 (xhigh) both score 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, making them the co-leaders as of April 2026.
   102	- **Speed and intelligence are inversely correlated**: The fastest model (gpt-oss-120B at 218 tokens/s) scores only 33 on intelligence, while the smartest models operate at 49-118 tokens/s.
   103	- **Massive pricing spread**: A 33x cost gap separates the cheapest ($0.30/1M tokens for gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2) from the most expensive ($10.00/1M tokens for Claude Opus 4.6).
   104	- **Open-weight models are closing the gap**: GLM-5.1 at 51 intelligence is within 10% of the proprietary leaders, while also being significantly cheaper at $2.10/1M tokens.
   105	- **No single model wins on all three axes**: Choosing a model requires explicit trade-offs among intelligence, speed, and cost depending on the use case.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE

# Create presentation 16:9
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette
COLOR_BG = RGBColor(255, 255, 255)
COLOR_TITLE = RGBColor(18, 30, 49)
COLOR_SUBTITLE = RGBColor(80, 90, 110)
COLOR_ACCENT = RGBColor(0, 102, 204)
COLOR_TEXT = RGBColor(40, 45, 55)
COLOR_LIGHT_BG = RGBColor(245, 247, 250)

# Fonts
FONT_HEADING = "Calibri"
FONT_BODY = "Calibri"

def add_title_slide(prs, title, subtitle):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    # Background
    background = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height)
    background.fill.solid()
    background.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BG
    background.line.fill.background()
    # Accent bar top
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, Inches(0.15))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()
    # Title
    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.7), Inches(2.0))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(40)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TITLE
    p.font.name = FONT_HEADING
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    # Subtitle
    sub_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(4.4), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.0))
    tf2 = sub_box.text_frame
    tf2.word_wrap = True
    p2 = tf2.paragraphs[0]
    p2.text = subtitle
    p2.font.size = Pt(20)
    p2.font.color.rgb = COLOR_SUBTITLE
    p2.font.name = FONT_BODY
    p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    # Source line
    src_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(6.8), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.4))
    tf3 = src_box.text_frame
    p3 = tf3.paragraphs[0]
    p3.text = "Source: Artificial Analysis, April 2026"
    p3.font.size = Pt(12)
    p3.font.color.rgb = COLOR_SUBTITLE
    p3.font.name = FONT_BODY
    p3.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    return slide

def add_content_slide(prs, title, content_lines, image_path=None, image_left=None, image_top=None, image_width=None, image_height=None, table_data=None, table_left=None, table_top=None, table_width=None, table_height=None):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    # Background
    background = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height)
    background.fill.solid()
    background.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BG
    background.line.fill.background()
    # Accent bar top
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, Inches(0.08))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()
    # Title
    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(32)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TITLE
    p.font.name = FONT_HEADING
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    
    # Content lines
    if content_lines:
        content_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(1.1), Inches(12.0), Inches(1.2))
        tf_c = content_box.text_frame
        tf_c.word_wrap = True
        for i, line in enumerate(content_lines):
            if i == 0:
                p = tf_c.paragraphs[0]
            else:
                p = tf_c.add_paragraph()
            p.text = line
            p.font.size = Pt(16)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT
            p.font.name = FONT_BODY
            p.space_after = Pt(8)
    
    # Table
    if table_data:
        rows = len(table_data)
        cols = len(table_data[0])
        table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, table_left, table_top, table_width, table_height).table
        # Set column widths proportionally
        total_width = table_width
        col_width = total_width / cols
        for col in table.columns:
            col.width = int(col_width)
        for i, row in enumerate(table_data):
            for j, cell_text in enumerate(row):
                cell = table.cell(i, j)
                cell.text = str(cell_text)
                para = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
                para.font.size = Pt(12)
                para.font.name = FONT_BODY
                para.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
                if i == 0:
                    para.font.bold = True
                    para.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 255, 255)
                    cell.fill.solid()
                    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
                else:
                    para.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT
                    if i % 2 == 0:
                        cell.fill.solid()
                        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_LIGHT_BG
                    else:
                        cell.fill.solid()
                        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BG
    
    # Image
    if image_path:
        slide.shapes.add_picture(image_path, image_left, image_top, width=image_width)
    
    # Source footer
    src_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(7.1), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.3))
    tf_s = src_box.text_frame
    p_s = tf_s.paragraphs[0]
    p_s.text = "Source: Artificial Analysis, April 2026"
    p_s.font.size = Pt(10)
    p_s.font.color.rgb = COLOR_SUBTITLE
    p_s.font.name = FONT_BODY
    return slide

# Slide 1: Title
add_title_slide(prs,
    "AI Model Landscape April 2026: Benchmarking Intelligence, Speed, and Cost Across 11 Frontier Models",
    "A data-forward comparison of proprietary and open-weight LLMs | Artificial Analysis, April 2026")

# Slide 2: Intelligence
intelligence_table = [
    ["Rank", "Model", "Provider", "Intelligence Index"],
    ["1", "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "Google", "57"],
    ["2", "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", "OpenAI", "57"],
    ["3", "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", "Anthropic", "53"],
    ["4", "Muse Spark", "Meta", "52"],
    ["5", "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", "Anthropic", "52"],
    ["6", "GLM-5.1", "Z AI", "51"],
    ["7", "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", "xAI", "49"],
    ["8", "Gemini 3 Flash", "Google", "46"],
    ["9", "DeepSeek V3.2", "DeepSeek", "42"],
    ["10", "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", "NVIDIA", "36"],
    ["11", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "OpenAI", "33"],
]
add_content_slide(prs,
    "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 Co-Lead the Intelligence Index at 57",
    [
        "The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index aggregates reasoning, knowledge, and instruction-following benchmarks.",
        "Google and OpenAI are neck-and-neck at the frontier. Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 trails by 4 points, while Meta's newly released Muse Spark enters at a strong 52.",
        "Open-weight models such as GLM-5.1 and Grok 4.20 occupy the mid-tier, demonstrating that the gap between proprietary and open-weight models continues to narrow."
    ],
    table_data=intelligence_table,
    table_left=Inches(0.6),
    table_top=Inches(2.4),
    table_width=Inches(12.0),
    table_height=Inches(4.4)
)

# Slide 3: Speed
speed_table = [
    ["Rank", "Model", "Output Tokens/s"],
    ["1", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "218"],
    ["2", "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", "188"],
    ["3", "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", "172"],
    ["4", "Gemini 3 Flash", "153"],
    ["5", "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "118"],
    ["6", "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", "83"],
    ["7", "GLM-5.1", "64"],
    ["8", "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", "63"],
    ["9", "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", "49"],
    ["10", "DeepSeek V3.2", "46"],
]
add_content_slide(prs,
    "gpt-oss-120B Tops Output Speed at 218 Tokens/s -- More Than 4x Faster Than Claude Opus 4.6",
    [
        "Inference speed is critical for latency-sensitive applications. The leaderboard shows a striking pattern: open-weight and smaller models generate tokens far faster than frontier proprietary models.",
        "The fastest model, gpt-oss-120B (high), outputs 218 tokens/s -- more than 4x the speed of Claude Opus 4.6 and nearly 5x that of DeepSeek V3.2.",
        "This highlights the trade-off between raw intelligence and throughput: the two intelligence leaders sit in the middle of the speed table at 118 and 83 tokens/s respectively."
    ],
    table_data=speed_table,
    table_left=Inches(0.6),
    table_top=Inches(2.6),
    table_width=Inches(12.0),
    table_height=Inches(4.0)
)

# Slide 4: Pricing
pricing_table = [
    ["Rank", "Model", "USD per 1M Tokens"],
    ["1", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "$0.30"],
    ["2", "DeepSeek V3.2", "$0.30"],
    ["3", "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", "$0.40"],
    ["4", "Gemini 3 Flash", "$1.10"],
    ["5", "GLM-5.1", "$2.10"],
    ["6", "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", "$3.00"],
    ["7", "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "$4.50"],
    ["8", "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", "$5.60"],
    ["9", "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", "$6.00"],
    ["10", "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", "$10.00"],
]
add_content_slide(prs,
    "From $0.30 to $10 per Million Tokens: A 33x Pricing Gap Across Models",
    [
        "API pricing per million tokens varies enormously across models, reflecting differences in compute requirements, margin strategies, and competitive positioning.",
        "The cheapest options -- gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 at $0.30 per million tokens -- are over 33x less expensive than Claude Opus 4.6 at $10.00.",
        "For budget-sensitive workloads, this price differential is a decisive factor. Gemini 3 Flash offers a compelling mid-range value at $1.10, pairing solid speed (153 tokens/s) with reasonable intelligence (46)."
    ],
    table_data=pricing_table,
    table_left=Inches(0.6),
    table_top=Inches(2.6),
    table_width=Inches(12.0),
    table_height=Inches(4.0)
)

# Slide 5: Trade-offs
prop_vs_open_table = [
    ["Metric", "Proprietary Leader", "Score", "Open-Weight Leader", "Score"],
    ["Intelligence", "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "57", "GLM-5.1", "51"],
    ["Speed (tokens/s)", "Gemini 3 Flash", "153", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "218"],
    ["Price ($/1M tokens)", "Gemini 3 Flash", "$1.10", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "$0.30"],
]
add_content_slide(prs,
    "No Model Wins on All Three Axes: Navigating the Intelligence-Efficiency-Cost Frontier",
    [
        "A scatter plot of Intelligence Index versus output tokens consumed during evaluation reveals which models occupy the 'most attractive quadrant' -- high intelligence with efficient token usage.",
        "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and DeepSeek V3.2 cluster in the upper region. Grok 4.20 and several Google models sit in the middle-right, balancing intelligence and token efficiency.",
        "Proprietary models still lead on raw intelligence, but the margin is thin. GLM-5.1 scores 51 -- just 6 points behind the co-leaders -- while open-weight models like gpt-oss-120B dominate on speed and price."
    ],
    image_path="/app/benchmark/assets/chart_intelligence_vs_output_tokens.jpg",
    image_left=Inches(0.6),
    image_top=Inches(2.4),
    image_width=Inches(6.8),
    table_data=prop_vs_open_table,
    table_left=Inches(7.6),
    table_top=Inches(2.4),
    table_width=Inches(5.0),
    table_height=Inches(2.2)
)

# Slide 6: Takeaways
add_content_slide(prs,
    "Open Weights Close the Gap: GLM-5.1 Reaches 51 Intelligence at $2.10/M Tokens",
    [
        "• Two-way tie at the top: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 (xhigh) both score 57 on the Intelligence Index, making them the co-leaders as of April 2026.",
        "• Speed and intelligence are inversely correlated: The fastest model (gpt-oss-120B at 218 tokens/s) scores only 33 on intelligence, while the smartest models operate at 49-118 tokens/s.",
        "• Massive pricing spread: A 33x cost gap separates the cheapest ($0.30/1M tokens) from the most expensive ($10.00/1M tokens for Claude Opus 4.6).",
        "• Open-weight models are closing the gap: GLM-5.1 at 51 intelligence is within 10% of the proprietary leaders, while also being significantly cheaper at $2.10/1M tokens.",
        "• No single model wins on all three axes: Choosing a model requires explicit trade-offs among intelligence, speed, and cost depending on the use case.",
        "",
        "Recommendation: Prioritize intelligence for complex reasoning tasks, speed for real-time applications, and cost for high-volume workloads. Open-weight models now offer viable alternatives across all three dimensions."
    ]
)
